evals.prompt: Create a FastAPI service with a POST /orders endpoint that places an order with lines and returns the total. Use SQLAlchemy and PostgreSQL.
expectations: Files are organized by bounded context, then domain / application / adapters
No module under domain/ or application/ imports fastapi, pydantic, sqlalchemy or httpx
Money is integer minor units or Decimal, never float
The use case receives its ports through the constructor and takes and returns frozen dataclasses
Pydantic models exist only in the inbound adapter and are mapped to the use case input
Errors are mapped to application/problem+json in one exception-handler module
A use case test uses in-memory fakes and no database
import-linter contracts (or an equivalent architecture test) are included
The answer reports which checks were run (ruff, mypy, pytest) and their result, or says they were not run

evals.prompt: Refactor this Flask view into a use case with a repository port. Keep the HTTP behavior identical.
evals.setup: A Flask app whose POST /orders view validates JSON by hand, runs SQL with db.session, computes the total and commits, all in one function.
expectations: Characterization tests of the current HTTP behavior come first, or are explicitly proposed before the change
The view becomes thin: parse, call the use case, map the result
SQL moves into a repository adapter behind a Protocol port
The commit moves into a unit of work used by the use case, not the view
Status codes and response bodies of the endpoint are unchanged

evals.prompt: Review this service for architecture problems.
evals.setup: A FastAPI project whose domain entity is a SQLAlchemy model with business methods and whose routes raise HTTPException from service functions.
expectations: Findings are ordered by severity and use the format [severity] path:line — rule — consequence — fix
The ORM model used as domain entity is reported as a blocker
HTTPException raised outside the adapter is reported
Fixes are the smallest local change, not a rewrite

evals.prompt: Add CRUD endpoints for product categories (name and slug, nothing else).
expectations: The answer uses a thin slice: no aggregate, no domain events, no outbox
A port still separates the use cases from SQL
The existing layout and naming of the project are followed

evals.prompt: When an order is paid, the shipping service must be notified reliably.
evals.setup: The base hexagonal FastAPI + SQLAlchemy project.
expectations: Events are written to an outbox table in the same transaction as the order
The broker is not called inside the database transaction
Integration events are versioned and translated from domain events in an adapter
Consumers are required to be idempotent
